_about: Models the matte sidecar can offer (matte.py reads this file; MATTE_MODELS picks ids from it). Segmenters (kind absent or "segmenter") are plain ONNX graphs executed by onnxruntime; the tracker (kind "tracker") is a SAM 2.1 checkpoint run by the pinned sam2 package on torch — no remote code either way. `urls` are tried in order (the pinned release asset first, then a mirror holding the byte-identical file); the download is verified against `sha256` before the file is used, and that sha256 is the `weights` the app folds into its memo keys. `offer` lists the devices a model is offered on by default (MATTE_MODELS can name a model for every device); `defaultFor` marks the device(s) whose default model it is (MATTE_DEFAULT_MODEL* override). The facts come from docs/reviews/background-removal-bench/models.json (research run 2026-10-08) and the SAM 2 prototype (2026-10-09).

isnet-anime.label: Anime (fast)
isnet-anime.upstream: SkyTNT/anime-segmentation (ISNet / DIS); the HF mirror is the author's own upload, byte-identical (same LFS sha256)
isnet-anime.notes: opset 11, input float32 [1,3,1024,1024], output [1,1,1024,1024] with the sigmoid in the graph; /255 then minus mean, std 1 (rembg dis_anime.py — NOT the ImageNet std). The 34 Resize nodes carry absolute sizes, so other input sizes are derived with tools/rescale_graph.py; fp16 on CUDA with tools/to_fp16.py (MAE 0.00005 vs fp32). Anime-style characters only: it detects nothing on photographic content. The CPU default (~130 ms/frame at 512² on 8 cores).

birefnet-lite.label: General (precise)
birefnet-lite.upstream: ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet, BiRefNet_lite (general-use training set, swin_v1_tiny backbone, epoch 232); rembg's ONNX export — no mirror with the same sha256 is known
birefnet-lite.notes: fixed batch 1, float32 [1,3,1024,1024] input, [1,1,1024,1024] LOGITS output (the sidecar applies the sigmoid); ImageNet mean/std. ORT's CUDA arena grows to 14.5 GB uncapped: it runs under gpu_mem_limit = MATTE_GPU_MEM_LIMIT_GIB (6.3 GB footprint at 6 GiB; 5/4/3 GiB caps FAIL). Session create 10–20 s on an RTX 5080, ~170 ms/frame; stable on a moving subject (IoU 0.96–0.99 every frame): the GPU default. Offered on the CPU too (fp32 1024², 3.7–10 s/frame at 12.6 GB RSS) but gated by 14 GiB of available RAM: below that it is listed unavailable with the figure, never silently absent.

sam2-tiny.label: Guided (click to select)
sam2-tiny.upstream: facebookresearch/sam2, SAM 2.1 hiera-tiny checkpoint (release 092824); run by the sam2 package pinned at commit 2b90b9f5ceec907a1c18123530e92e794ad901a4 (requirements-sam2.txt) with its own config configs/sam2.1/sam2.1_hiera_t.yaml
sam2-tiny.notes: A video object tracker, not a per-frame segmenter: POST /v1/track takes the whole clip (rgb24 at the tracking size, long side <= 1024) plus prompts (a box and/or clicks on one or more frames, or a mask — one 8-bit gray PNG record after the frames, Phase 5d: the per-frame model's matte of one good frame is the most reliable prompt, applied with add_new_mask; the frame's clicks refine it) and answers one binary mask per frame; POST /v1/track/frame answers one prompted frame's mask for the live overlay. Frames are resized to 1024² inside (image_size), bf16 autocast on CUDA (~35 ms/frame propagation + ~30 ms frame prep at 720², ~1.2 GB VRAM), fp32 on CPU (~1.5 s/frame). Built with add_all_frames_to_correct_as_cond=true so corrections on later frames stick; the CUDA connected-components extension is not built (SAM2_BUILD_CUDA=0) — hole filling (fill_hole_area=8) runs through scipy instead. The app gates a per-frame model's matte with this mask for the edges (DESIGN.md §4.3).
